root_cause.description: Unconditionally removed the road-level <link> element from every junction-connector road (road.junction != "-1"), regardless of whether the link was valid, under the undocumented premise 'Junction connectors should not have road-level links'. That premise is not supported by the manual reference map, this pipeline's own generator output, or the ASAM OpenDRIVE junction/connection model (the junction's <connection> element disambiguates routing among multiple connecting roads at the lane level; it does not substitute for the connecting road's own predecessor/successor road-level link, which is what lets road-by-road traversal consumers such as CARLA's Waypoint API cross the connector).

manual_reference_map.note: Junction-connector roads are the roads MOST likely (100%) to declare road-level links in the manual reference, not least -- directly contradicting the hardener's premise.

fix.behavior_change: Junction-connector road <link> elements are no longer unconditionally removed. Instead they are validated by the same target-existence rule already applied to ordinary roads: kept if the predecessor/successor references an existing road, removed (ROAD_LINK_REMOVED) only if the reference is dangling. _validate_junction_connector() (checking the connector appears in its junction's <connection> list) is unchanged.

not_a_spec_compliant_omission_because: Manual/RoadRunner-authored reference map: 725/725 (100%) of junction-connector roads declare road-level link.
This pipeline's own OSM-based generator: 22589/22589 (100%) of junction-connector roads on the current pin already declare road-level link before the hardener runs.
All declared links (both maps) are valid (predecessor_valid_rate / successor_valid_rate = 1.0) -- the hardener was not cleaning up dangling references, it was blanket-deleting correct data.
The junction's <connection> element and the connector road's own <link> serve different consumers (lane-level routing disambiguation vs. road-by-road traversal) and are not redundant.
